title: feat(minify): avoid removing the default value of the `filter` function
author: yisibl
summary: Stops omitting default arguments in filter functions (e.g. keeps `brightness(1)`) to work around bugs in very old Chrome (~49). The maintainer declined working around decade-old browser bugs, which is also in the project philosophy ("Limit hacks for very old browsers").
evidence: devongovett 2026-01-07: "Chrome 49 is almost 10 years old so I doubt anyone is targeting that anymore. But we could potentially check the targets and see if the minimum version is below that." devongovett 2026-03-09: "CSS correctness is one thing. It is another thing entirely to account for 10 year old browser bugs. There is no source of truth for that. When implementing things we need to rely on the spec being correct, otherwise the job is not possible." The PR disables the omission unconditionally, not target-gated.
draft:
Thanks for digging into these old Chrome bugs. As discussed above, we rely on the spec for what default arguments mean, and the affected versions (around Chrome 49) are about ten years old, so always keeping `brightness(1)` etc. would make output bigger for everyone to work around browsers that are basically no longer targeted. I'm going to close this. If you hit this with a browser that's still in real use, please open an issue with the browser version and a small example, and we can look at gating it on targets.
